expected_files.comment_de: Solldateien der Testvektoren (spec/testvectors/expected/<name>.json). exit_code und finding_classes gelten für die Prüfumgebung des Korpus (seit Fassung 1.4). Ab Fassung 1.10 kann eine Solldatei zusätzlich evidence_level (Prüfumgebung des Korpus) und auditor_inputs tragen (null, oder die Erwartung mit der Prüfumgebung pruefer_<name>.json des Vektors); das Schema nimmt Solldateien mit und ohne diese Member an. Die Verbundenheit steht im Objekt evidence_level. Bei einem unbrauchbaren Aufruf (Exit 3 ohne Bericht, Formatspezifikation 10.8) ist auditor_inputs.evidence_level null: Ohne Bericht gibt es keine Beweisstufe (10.9.2, 10.10.1).
expected_files.comment_en: Expected files of the test vectors (spec/testvectors/expected/<name>.json). exit_code and finding_classes hold for the corpus environment (since edition 1.4). From edition 1.10 an expected file may also carry evidence_level (corpus environment) and auditor_inputs (null, or the expectation with the vector's environment pruefer_<name>.json); the schema accepts expected files with and without these members. The affiliation lies in the object evidence_level. For an unusable invocation (exit 3 without a report, format spec 10.8) auditor_inputs.evidence_level is null: without a report there is no evidence level (10.9.2, 10.10.1).

conditions.comment: all seven codes when rated: the reason, or null when the condition is met

evidence_level.comment: null for an unusable invocation (exit_code 3 without finding classes), which writes no report and has no evidence level (format spec 10.8, 10.9.2, 10.10.1); the object of state format_error only for FORMAT_ERROR with a report

vendor_key_list.comment_de: Liste der Gegenzeichnungsschlüssel des Herstellers im Prüfpaket (Format-Spezifikation 10.7.1; bis Fassung 1.9 „Hersteller-Schlüsselliste“). Sie zählt nur, wenn ihre Signatur gegen eine Herstellerwurzel prüft, die der PRÜFER beibringt (7.1). Ab Fassung 1.10 nennt sie nur Schlüssel der Rolle countersigning und ist die Projektion der Rollenliste (key_role_list) auf diese Rolle; Format, Ort und Leseregeln bleiben, damit Verifier und Appliances der Fassung 1.9 sie weiter lesen.
vendor_key_list.comment_en: List of the vendor's countersigning keys in the verification package (format spec 10.7.1; up to edition 1.9 the vendor key list). It counts only if its signature verifies against a vendor root the AUDITOR supplies (7.1). From edition 1.10 it names only keys of role countersigning and is the projection of the role list (key_role_list) onto that role; format, place and reading rules stay, so that verifiers and appliances of edition 1.9 keep reading it.
vendor_key_list.signed_bytes: JCS (RFC 8785) of the list object without its member signatur; Ed25519 by the root key named in signatur.wurzel_id
vendor_key_list.valid_at: gueltig_ab <= server_ts, and server_ts < gueltig_bis if present, and server_ts < widerrufen_ab if present
vendor_key_list.auditor_supplied: from edition 1.10 the auditor may pass a list of this format himself (--vendor-key-list, auditor_inputs.inputs.vendor_key_list), for example the current one fetched from the vendor; format and reading rules stay unchanged; such a list establishes neither a receipt (format spec 7.1) nor an anchor history page (format spec 8.8.3); its keys belong to K_cs^L, the set the roles are checked against (format spec 10.7.4; 7.4.10, L1)
vendor_key_list.roles: from edition 1.10 the list names only keys of role countersigning (format spec 10.7.3), and the vendor never adds a key of another role: they sign receipts and, until ende_doppelbetrieb (format spec 10.7.5), the wrapper of licence statements, refusals and activation receipts and anchor history pages of kind v1; never a page of kind v2, the update manifest or a day entry of the vendor log; why it cannot carry roles: verifiers and appliances of edition 1.9 refuse every other member, and a list with a member for roles would be ineffective for them, so that every receipt whose key the auditor does not pin would give RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED
vendor_key_list.projection: the list of the same signing procedure names exactly the entries of role countersigning of the role list, with character for character equal key_id, pubkey, gueltig_ab, gueltig_bis and widerrufen_ab (key_role_list.projection); a vendor rule (heartbeat spec 9.11), not checked by the verifier
vendor_key_list.path_never_role_list: a role list never stands at keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json: there it would make this list ineffective, and every receipt whose key the auditor does not pin would give RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED (pinned keys keep precedence, format spec 7.1)
vendor_key_list.root_key: no entry names the public key of the vendor root: a rule for the vendor (heartbeat spec 9.11 item 1), not checked by the verifier on this list, so that a verifier from edition 1.10 refuses no list that a verifier of edition 1.9 accepts

key_role_list.comment_de: Rollenliste (Format-Spezifikation 10.7.2, ab Fassung 1.10): nennt jeden Schlüssel, mit dem der Hersteller im laufenden Betrieb signiert, mit genau einer Rolle (Format-Spezifikation 10.7.3), ausgenommen die Protokollschlüssel, die die Protokollschlüsselliste nennt. Die Herstellerwurzel signiert sie. Sie belegt nie eine Quittung (7.1); sie belegt Bescheidschlüssel für Seiten der Anker-Historie (8.8.3) und ist Grundlage der Rollenprüfung (10.7.4). Sie steht nie in einem Prüfpaket und nie unter keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json; der Prüfer übergibt sie mit --vendor-key-list.
key_role_list.comment_en: Role list (format spec 10.7.2, from edition 1.10): names every key the vendor signs with in running operation, with exactly one role (format spec 10.7.3), except the protocol keys, which the protocol key list names. The vendor root signs it. It never establishes a receipt (7.1); it establishes statements keys for anchor history pages (8.8.3) and is the basis of the role check (10.7.4). It is never in a verification package and never at keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json; the auditor passes it with --vendor-key-list.
key_role_list.signed_bytes: JCS (RFC 8785) of the list object without its member signatur; Ed25519 by the vendor root named in signatur.wurzel_id, from the auditor or built in and named (format spec 7.1), never from a package or an extract

version.comment: strictly increasing; a new version keeps every entry of earlier versions with the same key_id, pubkey and rolle; it may add or shorten their validity members

ausgestellt.comment: issue time, read after the grammar of format spec 10.7.1

ende_doppelbetrieb.comment: end of dual operation (format spec 10.7.5): from this instant keys of role countersigning sign receipts only; once present, every later version carries the same value

schluessel.comment: per key exactly key_id, pubkey, rolle, gueltig_ab and optionally gueltig_bis and widerrufen_ab, all strings; a key_id and a pubkey occur at most once each

key_role_list.reserved_rule: an entry with rolle protocol makes the list ineffective: protocol keys stand only in the protocol key list (format spec 7.4.7)
key_role_list.root_key_rule: an entry whose pubkey equals the public key of the root against which the signature is checked makes the list ineffective (reason format, verifier.key_roles); on the list of countersigning keys and on the protocol key list the same rule binds only the vendor and is not checked (format spec 10.7)
key_role_list.unknown_role: an entry with another, unknown rolle establishes nothing but counts for uniqueness and for the role check (note unknown_role, verifier.key_roles); new top-level members need a new format
key_role_list.valid_at: as vendor_key_list.valid_at (format spec 10.7.1), compared on nanoseconds
key_role_list.effective: only if every rule holds and the signature holds against a vendor root with this wurzel_id; which of several lists counts and whether a role contradicts is decided by format spec 10.7.4 (verifier.key_roles); an ineffective list establishes no key and is no finding, the report names the reason (key_roles)
key_role_list.selection: format spec 10.7.4 R1 and R2 (verifier.key_roles.steps): candidates are the distinct role lists from --vendor-key-list; the counting candidate with the largest version is effective; same version with different bytes, a dropped entry or a changed or dropped ende_doppelbetrieb: none is effective (lists_contradictory)
key_role_list.role_check: format spec 10.7.4 R3 (verifier.key_roles.steps): by public key against the list of countersigning keys (K_cs^L), the protocol key list and the pins; a public key in two roles makes the list ineffective (key_in_two_roles) or drops the pin
key_role_list.never_in_package: never in a verification package, never at keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json (there it would make the list of countersigning keys ineffective, and every receipt whose key the auditor does not pin would give RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED) and never inside ledger-ankerhistorie/2; the auditor passes it with --vendor-key-list (auditor_inputs.inputs.vendor_key_list)
key_role_list.projection: vendor rule, checked by the vendor's own tools and not by the verifier: the list of countersigning keys of the same signing procedure (vendor_key_list) names exactly the entries of role countersigning, with character for character equal key_id, pubkey, gueltig_ab, gueltig_bis and widerrufen_ab (heartbeat spec 9.11)
key_role_list.reserve: the vendor MUST name in every role list, besides the active statements key, a statements key in reserve whose private part is kept offline (heartbeat spec 9.11); the verifier does not check this
published_at: rollenliste.json and rollenliste/<version>.json at both places of publication
every installation and every update bundle

example.seed_rule: seed = SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes REKORDER-TESTVECTOR-KEY: followed by the seed name (as for the other test keys of the corpus)
example.comment: version 1 of the test corpus; its entries of role countersigning are the projection of version 1 of the corpus list of countersigning keys (test vector valid_vendor_list); signature by the root testwurzel-1 (format spec 10.7.2)

protocol_key_list.comment_de: Protokollschlüsselliste (Format-Spezifikation 7.4.7, ab Fassung 1.10): bestätigt die Protokollschlüssel des Herstellerprotokolls, signiert mit der Herstellerwurzel. Ihr Format ist ihre Rolle: Jeder ihrer Schlüssel hat die Rolle protocol (Format-Spezifikation 10.7.3) und steht in keiner anderen Liste. Sie steht nie in einem Prüfpaket und nie als keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json; ein Leser der Liste der Gegenzeichnungsschlüssel (vendor_key_list) nimmt sie nie an, und sie bestätigt nie einen Gegenzeichnungsschlüssel. Weder die Liste der Gegenzeichnungsschlüssel noch die Rollenliste (key_role_list) nennt die Protokollschlüssel.
protocol_key_list.comment_en: Protocol key list (format spec 7.4.7, from edition 1.10): confirms the protocol keys of the vendor log, signed with the vendor root. Its format is its role: every key in it has the role protocol (format spec 10.7.3) and stands in no other list. It is never in a verification package and never at keys/vendor/schluesselliste.json; a reader of the list of countersigning keys (vendor_key_list) never accepts it, and it never confirms a countersigning key. Neither the list of countersigning keys nor the role list (key_role_list) names the protocol keys.
protocol_key_list.signed_bytes: JCS (RFC 8785) of the list object without its member signatur; Ed25519 by the vendor root named in signatur.wurzel_id, from the auditor or built in and named (format spec 7.1), never from a package or an extract

version.comment: strictly increasing; a new version keeps every key ever listed, with its end of validity

ausgestellt.comment: issue time, read after the grammar of format spec 10.7

erster_tag.comment: start of the log; equal in every version

fuellerbindung.comment: filler commitment Hex(SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS({filler_secret: Hex(G), kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_commitment.v1, log_id})))) to the filler secret G of this log (vendor_log.fillers.filler_commitment) if the vendor derives its fillers, else null; once set, equal in every later version; the verifier reads it only for that rule (format spec 7.4.7, 7.4.10, L1 item 2)

orte.comment: places of publication; at least one outside the vendor's operation; they change only with a new version signed by the vendor root; what a reader can expect from a place outside the vendor's operation and how to check it: heartbeat spec 9.9

schluessel.comment: per key exactly as in format spec 10.7; a key_id and a pubkey occur at most once each

protocol_key_list.valid_at: gueltig_ab <= t, and t < gueltig_bis if present, and t < widerrufen_ab if present (format spec 10.7); against day entries gueltig_ab is not checked, and an entry under a key with gueltig_bis or widerrufen_ab counts only with a confirmed time stamp before the earlier of the two (format spec 7.4.10, L2 (e))
protocol_key_list.effective: only if every rule holds and the signature holds against a vendor root with this wurzel_id; which of several lists counts is decided by step L1; an ineffective list establishes no key and is no finding, the report names the reason
protocol_key_list.standby_key: the list SHOULD name a second protocol key whose private part is kept offline
protocol_key_list.uniqueness: key_id and pubkey of a protocol key occur in no version of the list of countersigning keys and of the role list; key_id and pubkey are unique over all versions of all three lists (heartbeat spec 9.9, 9.11)
protocol_key_list.root_key: no entry names the public key of the vendor root: a rule for the vendor (heartbeat spec 9.11 item 1) that the verifier does not check on this list (format spec 10.7)
protocol_key_list.role_check: the role check compares the effective list with the countersigning keys and with the effective role list (format spec 10.7.4, R3 (b) and (c); 7.4.10, L1 item 3)
published_at: keys.json at both places of publication

example.comment: fuellerbindung is the filler commitment of the published test filler secret (vendor_log.fillers.test_vectors.example.filler_commitment)

vendor_log.comment_de: Herstellerprotokoll (Format-Spezifikation 7.4, Heartbeat-Spezifikation §9.9, ab Fassung 1.10). Der Hersteller legt sich für jeden abgeschlossenen UTC-Tag mit einem signierten Tageseintrag auf die Menge seiner Gegensignaturen und Lückenzeugen fest; Zeitstempelstellen bezeugen die Festlegung. Das Protokoll ist eine Angabe des Prüfers: Nichts davon steht im Prüfpaket, in der Kette, in einer Quittung, im Manifest, in der Liste der Gegenzeichnungsschlüssel, in der Rollenliste oder in einer Nachricht der Appliance, und ein Verifier liest es nie aus dem Paket. Die Aufnahme einer Quittung in einen Tagesbaum belegt ihren Schlüssel nicht (Abschnitt 7.1).
vendor_log.comment_en: Vendor log (format spec 7.4, heartbeat spec 9.9, from edition 1.10). For every closed UTC day the vendor commits with a signed day entry to the set of its countersignatures and gap witnesses; time-stamping authorities witness the commitment. The log is an auditor input: none of it is in the verification package, the chain, a receipt, the manifest, the list of countersigning keys, the role list or an appliance message, and a verifier never reads it from the package. The inclusion of a receipt in a day tree does not establish its key (section 7.1).

hashes.leaf_hash: LH(x) = SHA-256(0x00 || x), x the leaf bytes of any length
hashes.mth: format spec 5; for the trees of the log additionally MTH([]) = SHA-256("")
hashes.inclusion: RFC 9162 section 2.1.3.2 exactly (verify_inclusion in format spec 5); the size comes from the signed day entry, never from the proof material
hashes.absence: for position p in a tree (n, R) strictly ordered by position, exactly one of: (i) n = 0 and no neighbour; (ii) one neighbour with index 0 and p below its position; (iii) one neighbour with index n - 1 whose position is below p; (iv) two neighbours with indices i and i + 1 and pos_i < p < pos_i+1; every neighbour leaf holds by inclusion against (n, R); positions compared as unsigned 32-byte values (= lowercase hex order)

countersignature.bytes: UTF-8(JCS({chain_id, merkle_root, server_ts, tree_size})): exactly the bytes the receipt signature covers (format spec 7.1); server_ts byte-identical to the receipt, with the fraction the server wrote

gap_witness.server_ts: the instant the server first recorded the gap witness, in exactly the characters the anchor history names in the row gap_witness of this root (the stored string, never a re-formatted time); it stays when the same root is presented again
gap_witness.comment: not signed on its own (the day entry commits to it); no appliance_id, no commitment, never the refusal statement; the member kind distinguishes it from every countersignature leaf with the same values
gap_witness.one_per_root: at most one gap witness per (chain_id, tree_size, merkle_root); a repeated presentation changes nothing and gives no further leaf (heartbeat spec 9.2)
gap_witness.refusal: never a leaf input; the refusal with which the server first records the witness carries exactly this server_ts string, a later refusal for the same root its own issue time (heartbeat spec 9.2, 9.5)

leaves.from_row: leaf(C, row) (format spec 7.4.2, Blatt aus der Aufzeichnung): from chain_id C and a row (tree_size, merkle_root, recorded_as, server_ts) of the anchor history, recorded_as countersigned gives the countersignature leaf and gap_witness the gap-witness leaf, each with exactly these values; reported gives no leaf; server_ts enters as the character string that record, row, extract or receipt carries, read only for day(server_ts) and for comparisons and never written anew; every leaf has at least 181 bytes
leaves.set_rule: the leaves of chain C on day d are every countersignature for C that left the server with day(server_ts) = d and every gap witness for C with day(server_ts) = d; they form a set (equal bytes count once); a repeated delivery of a stored original is the same leaf, a freshly issued repetition of a countersignature is a further leaf; a root recorded as gap witness and countersigned later gives two leaves, possibly on different days

reference_values.comment: format spec 7.4.2 (Blatt aus der Aufzeichnung): chain of test vector valid_sealed_export, tree_size 42, merkle_root = SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes LEDGER-BEISPIEL-WURZEL-42; leaf hashes LH(x) = SHA-256(0x00 || x)

rows.comment: the same root countersigned only on the following day

reformatted_server_ts.comment: the gap witness of row 0 with a re-formatted server_ts: another leaf, which the record does not hold (L6, VENDOR_LOG_DEFECTIVE)

negative.reported_row: a row reported gives no leaf
negative.refusal: a refusal with a later server_ts gives another leaf that is not in the record

chain_day.chain_root: RFC 6962 tree hash (format spec 5) whose leaf hashes are LH(leaf bytes) of the leaves of chain C on day d, ascending as unsigned 32-byte values of LH; LH is applied once; n >= 1; the order of roots in a record does not matter

position.appliance_id: the server: the appliance it bound the chain to; the verifier: GENESIS.appliance_id of the package

leaf.bytes: UTF-8(JCS({chain_root: Hex(chain_root(C, d)), kind, position: Hex(position(C, d))}))
leaf.comment: no chain_id, no size and no time; the day lies in the position; the kind ledger.vendor_log_day_leaf.v1 is that of every leaf of the day tree, a filler included, and says nothing about the origin of the leaf

day_tree.leaves: the chain-day leaves of all chains with leaves on day d and the fillers of day d (vendor_log.fillers); every leaf has the form and the kind ledger.vendor_log_day_leaf.v1 of a chain-day leaf
day_tree.order: strictly ascending by position (unsigned 32-byte compare = lowercase hex compare); no position twice
day_tree.root: RFC 6962 tree hash (format spec 5) whose leaf hashes are LH(leaf bytes) of the leaves of the day tree in this order; LH is applied once

empty_day.comment: tree_size 0; does not occur under the size rule (vendor_log.tree_size_rule), accepted by the verifier (format spec 7.4.10, L2 (g)) and used by test vectors

fillers.shape: exactly the form and kind of a chain-day leaf UTF-8(JCS({chain_root, kind: ledger.vendor_log_day_leaf.v1, position})); public data never tell a filler from the chain-day leaf of a chain; fillers are a leaf kind of their own, identifiable by their opening: the kind of a filler stands in the preimages of its position and chain_root
fillers.formation: not part of the check: no verifier reads, computes or checks a filler, and no check of the specification depends on how fillers are formed; fillers MUST be indistinguishable from chain-day leaves for the public; the derived formation below is the formation with which the vendor can show the origin of its fillers to an auditing party or a supervisory body (vendor_log.filler_opening), and the vendor SHOULD use it; using it, the protocol key list names its filler commitment, else fuellerbindung is null; the vendor may begin it later, with the first version of the list that names the commitment; for days before that version the origin of its fillers cannot be shown (format spec 7.4.4)
fillers.filler_secret: G: 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random generator, one per log, created offline in the signing procedure of the protocol key list before the first version of the list that names its filler commitment, and unchanged after that; held only by the protocol signing service, provided to it as a file; backed up offline at least twice; never published; if it becomes known the vendor states this publicly (heartbeat spec 9.9)
fillers.filler_commitment: SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS({filler_secret: Hex(G), kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_commitment.v1, log_id: L}))); member fuellerbindung of every version of the protocol key list from the first that names it (protocol_key_list.fields.fuellerbindung), public; G cannot be computed from it; whoever receives G checks it against the commitment and forms every day secret (vendor_log.filler_opening.filler_secret_check)
fillers.day_secret: g(d) = HMAC-SHA-256(G, UTF-8(JCS({day: d, kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_secret.v1, log_id: L}))); it depends only on log_id and day, not on the server_ts of the day entry
fillers.salt: s(d, i) = HMAC-SHA-256(g(d), UTF-8(JCS({index: i, kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_salt.v1}))), i = 0, 1, 2, ...
fillers.position: SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS({day: d, kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_position.v1, log_id: L, salt: Hex(s(d, i))})))
fillers.chain_root: SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS({day: d, kind: ledger.vendor_log_filler_root.v1, log_id: L, salt: Hex(s(d, i))})))
fillers.leaf: UTF-8(JCS({chain_root: Hex(root of candidate i), kind: ledger.vendor_log_day_leaf.v1, position: Hex(position of candidate i)}))
fillers.selection: the fillers of day d are exactly the candidates i = 0 to m(d) - 1, m(d) = tree_size(d) - n(d); no candidate is skipped; on a position collision (the position of a candidate meets that of a chain-day leaf or of another candidate, only on a SHA-256 collision) the closing does not close the day and raises an alarm; it forms no other fillers instead
fillers.order: mixed with the chain-day leaves, strictly ascending by position; the index i has no relation to the leaf index and enters no preimage of position or chain_root
fillers.day_binding: the day secret depends only on log_id and day: a day closed again after a destroyed entry (heartbeat spec 9.9, closing step 3) gets a new server_ts but the same candidates; two trees of one day share their fillers and side by side show only the leaves in which they differ (were the fillers bound to server_ts, two trees of one day would share only their chain-day leaves and together show which leaves are fillers); re-signing the same statement_jcs with another protocol key keeps every filler
fillers.not_public_comment: in no day entry, day leaves, extract, record, /v1/status, statistic or operations log; the filler commitment is public; the stored day leaves suffice to rebuild every record; the filler secret is needed only for an opening (vendor_log.filler_opening)
fillers.verifier: reads no filler secret, day secret, salt or opening and never tells a filler from a chain-day leaf

test_vectors.filler_secret_source: SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes LEDGER-TESTVEKTOR-FUELLERGEHEIMNIS
test_vectors.comment: published: a log whose fillers come from it hides nothing; test vectors use smaller trees than the size rule asks for, and their protocol key lists are signed by a root in published_test_keys

tree_of_5.comment: the chain of the 7.4.5 example (position b1ed9cae...2c04, chain_root b48375ab...b2ea) and the candidates 0 to 3; leaf order: candidate 3, candidate 2, candidate 0, the chain, candidate 1; the day entry of vendor_log.day_entry.example carries server_ts 2026-01-02T00:05:00.000Z

reclose.comment: a new closing of the same day with another server_ts of the day entry: the day secret does not depend on it, so the fillers and the root stay

padded_day.comment: the same day and chain under the size rule: 1023 fillers

tree_size_rule.rule: tree_size(d) is the smallest power of two that is at least 1024 and at least n(d), n(d) the number of chains with leaves on day d; the other m(d) = tree_size(d) - n(d) leaves are fillers
tree_size_rule.applies_to: every day entry of kind ledger.vendor_log_day.v1, so the rule is fixed before the first day of every log
tree_size_rule.exempt: logs whose protocol key list is signed by a root in published_test_keys (test vectors); such a log hides nothing
tree_size_rule.verifier_comment: the verifier checks the size only against the signed day entry and reports neither a size-rule nor a derivation violation (format spec 7.4.10)
tree_size_rule.observer_check: day leaves check (d); whether the size is the smallest admissible one shows only a whole-day opening together with proof of origin for every leaf that is not a filler of the selection (vendor_log.filler_opening, F3, F4)
tree_size_rule.reveals_de: nur, ob an dem Tag mehr als 1024 Ketten Blätter hatten, und dann die Zweierpotenz, die ihre Zahl nach oben begrenzt; überschreitet die Zahl eine Zweierpotenz, zeigt die Größe an diesem Tag Wachstum
tree_size_rule.reveals_en: only whether more than 1024 chains had leaves on the day and, if so, the power of two that bounds their number from above; when the number crosses a power of two, the size shows growth on that day
tree_size_rule.no_public_count: no public output of the vendor (status, statistics, operations logs) shows the number of chains or fillers of a day

statement_jcs.comment: the day entry in JCS form (RFC 8785), printable ASCII; only these UTF-8 bytes are signed

server_key_id.comment: a protocol key of the vendor log (format spec 7.4.7), never a key of another role (format spec 10.7.3)

server_signature.comment: Ed25519 by that protocol key over the UTF-8 bytes of statement_jcs

day_entry.wrapper_comment: the wrapper of heartbeat spec 9.4 without the reading copy statement
day_entry.signing: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, no prehash, no context) by a protocol key over UTF-8(statement_jcs); checked like the signature of a receipt (format spec 7.1)
day_entry.day_hash: SHA-256(UTF-8(statement_jcs)); compared at the head of the log, input of the next prev_hash and, for sha256, the imprint of the time stamps
day_entry.identity: the content: the same statement_jcs under two protocol keys is one entry; two different statement_jcs for one day of one log are a contradiction (VENDOR_LOG_CONTRADICTION); a pooled object keeps the set of its distinct pairs (server_key_id, server_signature), to which every element of additional_signatures with alg ed25519 belongs as the pair (key_id, signature), and no pair displaces another, whatever the order in which the files are passed
day_entry.prev_hash_covers: the content, not the signature or the time stamps
day_entry.gapless: exactly one entry per day from first_day on, also for a day without leaves
day_entry.running_tree_comment: this edition keeps no tree over the day entries; the days are linked by prev_hash alone

day.comment: the UTC day the entry closes

first_day.comment: start of the log; equal to erster_tag of the protocol key list

log_id.comment: equal to log_id of the protocol key list; a log for trials starts with staging-

prev_hash.comment: Hex(SHA-256(UTF-8(statement_jcs))) of the entry for the previous day; 64 zeros if and only if day = first_day

root.comment: Hex(root(day)); for tree_size 0 the SHA-256 value of the empty byte string

server_ts.comment: the instant the vendor's signing service fixes before it forms the entry (heartbeat spec 9.9), exactly YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ; MUST be at least end(day); the fillers do not depend on it (format spec 7.4.4)

tree_size.comment: number of leaves of the day tree

example.comment: day tree of a test log from one chain and four fillers (vendor_log.fillers.test_vectors.example.tree_of_5)

time.closing_delay_comment: the closing of day d does not start before end(d) + 300000 by the closing job's clock (heartbeat spec 9.9)
time.token_min_offset_comment: a time stamp witnesses d only with genTime >= end(d) + 60000; an earlier one shows that the day was closed too early
time.publication_offset_comment: P: the entry stands at both places by end(d) + P, 06:00 UTC of the following day; from then on d is due for the verifier: due(d) iff now >= end(d) + P
time.token_window_comment: W, 48 hours: a time stamp witnesses d only with genTime < end(d) + W
time.clock_alarm_comment: the closing job compares its clock with every genTime and with the server_ts of every newly signed result of the signing service (a repetition carries the recorded server_ts and must lie at most 60 seconds after the job's clock); a deviation of more than 60 seconds raises an alarm and stops closing

tokens.imprint: H(UTF-8(statement_jcs)) with the token's algorithm sha256, sha384 or sha512
tokens.vendor_must: the vendor MUST have every day stamped by at least two time-stamping authorities of different operators, none operated by the vendor or by a party affiliated with it (heartbeat spec 9.9, 9.10, 12); each request SHOULD carry certReq = true and a nonce; the verifier does not check who operates an authority
tokens.qualified_optional: one of the authorities MAY be one whose token declares itself qualified (rule QS, format spec 7.5.6); its time stamp is judged like any other and can witness the day; whether it chains to a root the auditor passes for the log and names as qualified is read only by condition log_day_qualified of the evidence level (format spec 10.9.1), the second way to level 3; per_day_object_max stays 4

timing.gen_time_ms: genTime truncated to whole milliseconds (format spec 2)

tokens.transitive_bound_comment: a day counts only by its own witnessing time stamp

extract.embedded: extracts embedded in an anchor history container count as files with the bytes UTF-8(JCS(element))

chain_id.comment: null only with empty chain_days (the mirror extract <YYYY>.json at the places of publication)

protocol_keys.comment: a protocol key list (protocol_key_list), judged after format spec 7.4.7, not by this grammar

additional_signatures.comment: format spec 7.4.8 (from edition 1.10): further signatures over UTF-8(statement_jcs); alg ed25519 carries a hex128 signature of a protocol key and is treated like the pair from entry (step L2 (a), (b)); any other alg is a seal this edition does not check, counted in vendor_log.days.signatures_not_checked; two equal elements violate the grammar; the generated schema does not express the two grammar rules (hex128 for ed25519, no equal elements), the verifier checks them at L0; a seal longer than 1024 characters needs a new format

server_ts.comment: a value of type rfc3339, copied byte for byte from the receipt or the recording; from edition 1.10 the server writes it as YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ (heartbeat spec 9.1, 9.2), another form does not violate this grammar

grammar_rules: exactly these members at every level, except inside protocol_keys; format is the constant
chain_id is null only with an empty chain_days
in every chain-day record exactly one of present and absent is not null
the roots of a record are pairwise distinct by their leaf bytes; a file carries at most one record per day; neighbours ascend by leaf_index
all extracts of one invocation name the same log_id
extract.authenticates: unsigned container of self-authenticating parts: day entries by protocol key and time stamps, chain-day records by inclusion under a witnessed day tree; not a statement of the vendor

leaves.comment: one pair [position, chain_root] per leaf of the day tree, in tree order

checks: (b) the number of pairs is tree_size of the day entry
(c) MTH over the leaves UTF-8(JCS({chain_root, kind: ledger.vendor_log_day_leaf.v1, position})) in this order is root of the witnessed day entry
(d) tree_size of the day entry is a power of two and at least 1024 (size rule, vendor_log.tree_size_rule), for every log whose protocol key list is not signed by a root in published_test_keys
day_leaves.checks_comment: a violation of (a) to (d) under a witnessed entry is a rule violation anyone can attribute to the vendor; beyond the tree size the day leaves reveal nothing: positions depend on the appliance_id, chain-day roots are hash values, and fillers cannot be told from chains without their opening

day_secret.comment: the day secret g(day); opens the whole day

filler_count.comment: m(day); not null exactly when day_secret is not null

fillers.comment: fillers opened one by one, pairwise distinct; at least one when day_secret is null

prose_rules: filler_count is not null exactly when day_secret is not null
fillers is not empty when day_secret is null
the salts of fillers are pairwise distinct
checks: F1 log_id and day equal those of the day entry; the entry is witnessed (format spec 7.4.6), and the day leaves pass the checks (a) to (c) of vendor_log.day_leaves against it
F2 for every element of fillers, position and root, formed after vendor_log.fillers from day, log_id and salt, stand as a pair in the day leaves

F3 with day_secret: the candidates formed from day_secret; candidates 0 to filler_count - 1 stand with their pairs in the day leaves, with pairwise distinct positions; the position of candidate filler_count stands nowhere in the day leaves; every salt in fillers is that of one of the candidates 0 to filler_count - 1; else the opening fails; a leaf at a candidate's position with another root under a witnessed entry has no provable origin, which is attributable to the vendor

F4 with day_secret: tree_size is the smallest power of two that is at least 1024 and at least tree_size - filler_count; if F4 fails the opening still stands and the vendor violated the size rule that day; if F4 passes, the size rule is not yet shown

outside the selection: a leaf that F2 shows to be a filler at a position that none of the candidates 0 to filler_count - 1 of an opening of the same day passing F3 occupies is a violation of the selection attributable to the vendor
filler_opening.filler_secret_check: with the filler secret G itself: the filler commitment from G equals fuellerbindung of the protocol key list; then every day secret is formed from G, filler_count per day is the smallest index of a candidate whose position is not in the day leaves, and F3 and F4 run for every day; the recipient learns for every day what a whole-day opening shows
filler_opening.check_tools: the derivation and F2 to F4 need only HMAC-SHA-256 and SHA-256; F1 needs the time-stamp profile (format spec 7.5)
filler_opening.authenticates: unsigned; self-authenticating against the witnessed day entry and the day leaves; never an auditor input of format spec 10.8 and never read by a verifier

shows.F2: every opened leaf is a filler and no chain-day leaf of a chain, formed from this salt when the witnessed tree was built; neither its index nor the number of fillers of the day
shows.F3: the candidates 0 to filler_count - 1 are fillers and candidate filler_count is not in the tree; for the number of chains only the upper bound n(d) <= tree_size - filler_count; not that the other leaves are not fillers (further candidates beyond filler_count or leaves from arbitrary salts go unnoticed), and not that they belong to chains with honest leaves, which the vendor shows per leaf with the chain's leaves and its appliance binding (customer data, heartbeat spec 12; no format in this edition)
shows.F4: a failed F4 shows a violation of the size rule; a passed F4 shows nothing without proof of origin for every leaf that is none of the candidates 0 to filler_count - 1
shows.every_opening: nothing about other days, and not that the day secret derives from the filler secret; only the filler secret itself, checked against the filler commitment, shows that (no evidence produced by LEDGER for days not opened)

filler_opening.size_rule_and_count: the size rule and the number of chains of a day are shown only by the whole-day opening together with proof of origin for every leaf that is not a filler of the selection
filler_opening.reveals: a whole-day opening shows its recipient, for a vendor keeping to the selection, the number of chains of the day, otherwise an upper bound; single fillers only that there are at least as many fillers as opened; an opening is bound to no recipient and can be passed on
filler_opening.recording: every opening is recorded with day, scope, recipient and time, from the start of the access chain as an entry DATA_ACCESS with data_class chain, purpose audit and access_mode export (heartbeat spec 9.9, 12)

reference_values.comment: the day tree of size 5 of vendor_log.fillers.test_vectors.example.tree_of_5, F1 assumed
reference_values.whole_day_count_4: passes F3; F4 fails, as expected for a test tree below the size rule
reference_values.whole_day_count_3: fails F3 (candidate 3 stands in the day leaves)

metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/keys/roles: the current role list (key_role_list, heartbeat spec 9.11)
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/keys/countersigning: the current list of countersigning keys (vendor_key_list, heartbeat spec 9.11)
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/log/head: the most recent published day as {"entry": ..., "timestamps": [...], "additional_signatures": [...]}
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/log/day/<YYYY-MM-DD>: this day in the same form
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/log/leaves/<YYYY-MM-DD>: the day leaves ledger-tagesblaetter/1 of this day
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/log/extract?chain_id=<uuid>[&fro: an extract ledger-protokollauszug/1 for this chain over at most 31 days
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/access-chain: the access chain statement ledger-zugriffskette/1 (heartbeat spec 12, access chain, item 9)
metadata_server_routes.GET /v1/access-chain/day/<YYYY-MM-DD>: the day head of the access chain for this day: the countersignature (heartbeat spec 9.1, all six members) of the access chain with the greatest tree_size among those with day(server_ts) <= this day, or null

routes.unknown_chain: HTTP 404 unknown_chain as in heartbeat spec 9.7

place_files.rollenliste/<version>.json: every version of the role list
place_files.schluesselliste.json: the current list of countersigning keys
place_files.leaves/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json: the day leaves of this day
place_files.<YYYY>.json: mirror extract of the year: an extract with chain_id null and empty chain_days carrying every day object of the year
place_files.verluste.json: the statements of lost leaves: a JSON array, only appended to, [] without a loss, from erster_tag on, of {"von": rfc3339, "bis": rfc3339, "angegeben": rfc3339, "grund": string}; von and bis in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ, both bounds included; grund names no customers, chains or persons; no number of leaves; the verifier does not read it (heartbeat spec 9.9, restore, item 2)
place_files.zugriffskette/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json: the day head of the access chain for this day

routes.access_rule: requests under /v1/log/ and /v1/anchors are not recorded: no chain_id, no appliance_id and no source address beyond the rate limiter in memory (heartbeat spec 12 item 7)
place_2_rules: the history of the place is protected against overwriting and deletion; every change is an addition a reader recognises as such

the credential with which the feed reaches place 2 can only add and cannot change the protection; nor can it trigger a job at the provider that may do more than the credential itself, for instance an integration workflow with write permissions of its own
a monitoring compares every state of place 2 with the previous one and alarms the vendor on every change that is not an addition and on every deletion
a time stamp or an additional signature that arrives later, and every new statement in verluste.json, is added as an addition, never by rewriting the history

every reader MAY keep own copies and compare with them; whoever holds the account at the hosting provider can lift the protection, which a reader notices only by comparison with an earlier copy (no evidence produced by LEDGER)
routes.places_comment: the protocol key list names both places in orte, one in the vendor's operation and one outside it, except for a log whose log_id begins with staging- whose places MAY both lie in the vendor's operation (heartbeat spec 9.9); both carry the files of place_files under the base address in orte, an address being <place>/<path>; a place MUST NOT end with / nor contain ? or #, which the signing procedure of the list checks (an auditor drops a trailing /); the metadata_server_routes are served by the metadata server in addition and are not a place; this specification names no place

access_chain_publication.start: at the latest on the earlier of erster_tag of the vendor log and the day on which a server of edition 1.10 first operates; stated beforehand in the statement

access_chain_publication.time_witness: the access chain MUST carry at least one time witness per day from an authority operated neither by the vendor nor by a party affiliated with it (format spec 7.3)
access_chain_publication.audit: mandatory at least once a year while an access chain exists: recompute the case-record commitments (account directory additions included), compare every day head with the package (t <= N and root(t) = merkle_root) and check for every day in the day leaves whether the position of the access chain stands on a day for which the package carries no receipt (then the chain is truncated or rewritten); the verifier does none of this

receipt_classes.comment: receipts of L8 (the same set in L7 and for r5'): every CHECKPOINT_RECEIPT whose signature holds under format spec 7.1 and that has no RECEIPT_INVALID, also with a contradiction or fork of the chain; cases of format spec 7.4.10 L8 in order: before_start (F known, d < F); future (server_ts in whole ms after now + 900000); d usable (included, not_included, unchecked no_record / record_failed / record_contradictory); c(d) determined, not witnessed (unchecked day_not_witnessed); S(d) not empty, c(d) undetermined (unchecked day_contradictory); S(d) empty (missing if due, else pending); after L2 (f) ended the check every receipt is unchecked first_day_contradictory

protocol_key_rules.l1_runs: step L1 runs at format spec 10.5 step 4 as soon as a protocol key list or a protocol key pin is supplied, with or without an extract; without an extract it reports no finding and only determines the protocol keys for format spec 7.1 and 8.8.3
protocol_key_rules.dropped_key: a counting candidate that lacks a key (same key_id with the same pubkey) of a counting candidate of a smaller version makes no list effective (reason lists_contradictory)
protocol_key_rules.role_check: by public key only (format spec 10.7.4, R3): an effective list sharing a public key with a countersigning pin, with K_cs^L or with the effective role list makes no list effective (reason key_in_two_roles); a protocol pin whose public key equals that of a key of K_cs^L or of the effective role list is dropped; an equal key_id alone is no role conflict; if no list is effective and every protocol pin was dropped (format spec 10.7.4 R3 (d)), the reason of L1 item 4 is key_in_two_roles, not no_list
protocol_key_rules.order_of_l2: L2 (a) to (e) for every object, then (f) determines F, then (g) and (h) for every object that passed (a) to (e)
protocol_key_rules.pins_only_first_day: with pins only: the common first_day of the objects that passed (a) to (e); none passed: F unknown without a finding; different values: one VENDOR_LOG_CONTRADICTION without day, F unknown, no object established, L2 (g), (h), L3 to L7 and L9 dropped, every receipt unchecked first_day_contradictory, first_day null
protocol_key_rules.signature_pairs: an object is established only if a pair under an established key holds (L2 b); every failing pair under an established key gives VENDOR_LOG_DEFECTIVE without removing the object; L2 (e) holds if one holding pair's key has no end or a confirmed time stamp shows a genTime before that key's end, compared to the nanosecond with the full genTime
protocol_key_rules.day_of: dayOf(o) reads statement_jcs as an I-JSON object with duplicate member names refused; the member day if it satisfies the grammar of type date (an existing calendar day, years 0001 to 9999), else no day; the log range 2000-01-01 to 9998-12-31 is not part of dayOf but a content rule checked in L2 (c), so a signed entry with day 1999-12-31 gets its VENDOR_LOG_CONTRADICTION on that day and counts in days.contradictory
protocol_key_rules.contradiction_scope_for_level: condition receipts_logged of the evidence level counts only VENDOR_LOG_CONTRADICTION findings without day or on a day of [Lo, T] (L7)
protocol_key_rules.same_in_every_version: no list is effective (reason lists_contradictory) if two counting candidates name different log_id or erster_tag, if two counting candidates name different fuellerbindung other than null, or if a counting candidate names fuellerbindung null and one of a smaller version a value (format spec 7.4.10, L1 item 2); fuellerbindung null in every candidate, or null up to a version and from that version on one value, makes no contradiction

auditor_inputs.comment_de: Angaben des Prüfers (Format-Spezifikation 2, 10.8, ab Fassung 1.10). Der Verifier liest sie als Bytes beim Aufruf, bevor er das Paket öffnet; im Browser gilt dasselbe für die Optionen. Dateien des Prüfers sind I-JSON nach Abschnitt 2, UTF-8 ohne Byte-Order-Mark, und ihre Objekte sind geschlossen. Ein Verstoß gegen eine Grammatik oder Grenze, eine Angabe, die öfter vorkommt als erlaubt, und jeder andere Bedienfehler ist ein unbrauchbarer Aufruf: Exit 3 mit Begründung auf der Fehlerausgabe, ohne Bericht. Ausgenommen ist der Vergleich des Anforderungszeitpunkts mit verify_args.json, der FORMAT_ERROR ergibt (Abschnitt 10.5). Was ein Mangel im Inhalt einer Angabe bewirkt, die ihre Grammatik einhält, bestimmen die Abschnitte 7.4, 8.8 und 10.7; es ist nie Exit 3. Nichts davon steht in einem Prüfpaket.
auditor_inputs.comment_en: Auditor inputs (format spec 2, 10.8, from edition 1.10). The verifier reads them as bytes at invocation, before it opens the package; in the browser the same holds for the options. Auditor files are I-JSON after section 2, UTF-8 without byte order mark, and their objects are closed. A violation of a grammar or limit, an input given more often than allowed and every other usage error is an unusable invocation: exit 3 with a reason on the error output, without a report. The exception is the comparison of the request time with verify_args.json, which gives FORMAT_ERROR (section 10.5). What a defect in the content of an input that keeps its grammar causes is decided by sections 7.4, 8.8 and 10.7; it is never exit 3. None of this is in a verification package.

file_rules.json: I-JSON (format spec 2): no member name twice, the number rule, no lone surrogates
file_rules.objects: closed: no members other than the defined ones
file_rules.violation: unusable invocation unless the section of the file says otherwise

unusable_invocation.browser_unknown_option: from edition 1.10 the browser edition answers an unknown option name with an error message instead of a verdict
unusable_invocation.command_line: from edition 1.10: the flags stand before the package and begin with two dashes, -- ends them; a flag without a value (--json, --now-from-package) takes none, a flag with a value takes it as --flag value or --flag=value, the value being the next argument even if it begins with a dash; --version stands alone; an argument before -- that begins with a dash is a flag, so a package with such a name stands after --; any other form (one dash, a value on a flag without one, a flag or a further argument after the package, an abbreviation) and a request for help (--help, -h, which names the flags on the error output) are usage errors (format spec 10.8)

auditor_inputs.older_verifiers: a verifier from edition 1.10 that does not know an input refuses the invocation (browser edition: an error message, also for an unknown option name) and never judges the package otherwise; verifiers of edition 1.9 do not all refuse: the Go verifier 1.9 refuses an unknown flag (exit 3) but accepts a repeated --tsa-root and reads only the last file, and passes over blocks that are not a certificate; the second verifier 1.9 exits with code 2 of its argument parser; the browser edition 1.9 passes over unknown options without a word and judges the package without them, and tsaRootsPem as a list aborts it; whoever passes one of these inputs or repeats --tsa-root MUST use a verifier from edition 1.10, and a tool or page that passes them MUST first query its version (--version, ledgerVerifyVersion)
auditor_inputs.earlier_inputs: the inputs of earlier editions (check time, expected roots, vendor root and pinned keys after format spec 7.1, verify_args.json) keep their rules; from edition 1.10 --vendor-key pins only a countersigning key (format spec 10.7.4): a pin whose public key the effective role list names with another role is dropped (R3 (d)), and a pin equal in key_id or pubkey to a pin of another role is an unusable invocation

freshness_window.comment: the freshness window of format spec 8.5: a whole number from 1 to 999999 without a leading zero, directly followed by the unit; any other form (0, a sign, a fraction, two units, a missing unit) is an unusable invocation; compared in whole milliseconds (format spec 2)

tsa_root.comment: repeatable from edition 1.10; every file counts

vendor_log_key.rules: two pins with one key_id and different keys, or a pin equal in key_id or pubkey to a pin of another role (--vendor-key for countersigning, --vendor-statement-key for statements), are an unusable invocation (7.4.10 L0, 10.7.4)

vendor_statement_key.rules: a pin not of the form key_id=hex64, two pins with one key_id and different keys, or a pin equal in key_id or pubkey to a pin of another role (--vendor-key, --vendor-log-key), are an unusable invocation (10.7.4); a pin whose public key a list names with another role is dropped (10.7.4, R3 (d))

vendor_key_list.rules: I-JSON; another or a missing format is an unusable invocation; the content is judged by format spec 10.7.1, 10.7.2 and 7.4.7: a list that does not hold is ineffective (named in the report), never exit 3

requested_at.grammar: rfc3339 as for the check time, any fractional seconds, compared in whole milliseconds (fraction cut)
requested_at.rules: optional; MUST NOT lie after the check time: against --now or the system clock checked at invocation (exit 3 without report), against the check time from verify_args.json at the start of stage 5 (FORMAT_ERROR, exit 3); never supplied from manifest.created_ts, verify_args.json, the check time or a clock; given without an anchor history it is accepted with the note requested_at_unused; without it completeness from the anchor history is not established (reason no_request_time) and level 3 of the evidence level is not reached (format spec 8.8.1, 10.9)

strict_pem.trailing_blanks: spaces and tabs at the end of a line do not count
strict_pem.outside_blocks: text outside a block is passed over (RFC 7468), lines with : outside a block included
strict_pem.content: the joined content lines follow grammar B64 (types.b64) and give exactly one certificate after Z.1 (verifier.timestamp_profile.z1_certificates)
unusable: a block with another label after BEGIN
a header line inside a block (a line with : between BEGIN and END)
a file without a CERTIFICATE block
strict_pem.every_block_counts: no block is passed over silently, and every repeated input counts
strict_pem.every_certificate_counts: every certificate of the file counts as a root of its purpose; a bundle file of many roots makes every one count (format spec 11.2)

stand.comment: when the auditor compiled the file, grammar of format spec 10.7

quelle.comment: where the auditor took it from

zertifikat.comment: base64 after B64 of a DER certificate after Z.1 with at most 16384 bytes

rules: two entries with a byte-identical certificate make the input ambiguous: exit 3
qualifiziert_bis, if present, lies after qualifiziert_ab, else exit 3

a root of the file counts for the purpose qualified only for tokens with qualifiziert_ab <= genTime < qualifiziert_bis (the upper bound only if present), compared as instants on nanoseconds; for the purpose chain it always counts
the report outputs stand and quelle
deriving the file from a trusted list is a step of the auditor; the verifier reads no signed XML lists

page.comment: the body of the HTTP response unchanged (heartbeat spec 9.7)

statement.comment: the unsigned reading copy; any JSON value, not evaluated

vendor_log.comment: extracts of the vendor log carried unchanged; each counts as a --vendor-log file with the bytes UTF-8(JCS(element))

anchor_history_file.content_check: the content of statement_jcs is checked only by step H2; a defect there never gives exit 3
